exposure: Mothers' perceptions of their birth experiences
cohort: The study included 350 mothers with a mean age of 30.10 years who underwent either vaginal delivery or unplanned cesarean section in a maternity hospital in Ankara.
finding: A weak negative relationship was found between mothers' perceptions of birth and postpartum breastfeeding success, suggesting that more positive birth perceptions were associated with lower breastfeeding success.
cross-section timing: Postpartum, with data collected between April 1, 2022 and May 1, 2022, but specific postpartum day/week not mentioned.
